messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] 2-QTL scans sapping memory/giving amazing LOD scores
parts:
scantwo requires a great deal of memory, especially, as in your case, with a very large number of markers.

Regarding the extremely large LOD scores, such things generally occur in the case of outliers in the phenotype, or a highly skewed phenotype distribution. I would focus on Haley-Knott regression (method="hk").

karl


On Feb 15, 2013, at 7:32 PM, Zhihao <tanz...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi!
>
> I've just started using R/qtl (and so have much to learn), and everything has been going great so far till I tried to run a 2-QTL scan (scantwo) on one of my crosses.
>
> This cross consists of 479 individuals, 1252 markers and is a "backcross" (actually it's a yeast haploid cross). Running scanone with different models and methods works fine, but when I start running scantwo, weird things happen.
>
> If I run a binary model with EM (which should be the most accurate for my phenotype), R/qtl saps all my memory (~2G) before crashing. This happens even when I run it on a single chromosome. If I run a normal model with EM, it manages to finish the run but I get LOD scores of 3000+. These are almost always between consecutive markers, and I suspect might have something to do with the small number of recombinants at these markers coupled with a drastic change in phenotypic means.
>
> I'm guessing I do have a larger number of individuals and markers, but I don't think R/qtl would drain all my memory when running scantwo? (I have successfully run scantwo on a cross about half the size and half the markers) Or might there be something fundamentally wrong with my data?
>
> Thanks for your time, and I'll be glad to provide more info if needed!
>
> Regards,
> Zhihao
